rules.cwe_name: Improper Encoding or Escaping of Output
rules.description: Replacing a substring with itself has no effect and may indicate a mistake.
An expression that has no effect and is used in a void context is most likely redundant and may indicate a bug.
Separately checking the state of a file before operating on it may allow an attacker to modify the file between the two operations.

rules.cwe_name: Creation of Temporary File With Insecure Permissions
rules.description: Creating a temporary file that is accessible by other users can lead to information disclosure and sometimes remote code execution.

rules.cwe_name: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in a Command ('Command Injection')
rules.description: Externally influenced data changes the syntax or meaning of a command sent to a downstream command interpreter.
Assigning to a property of a primitive value has no effect and may trigger a runtime error.
Using cookies without CSRF protection may allow malicious websites to submit requests on behalf of the user.
Prepending a backslash to an ordinary character in a string does not have any effect, and may make regular expressions constructed from this string behave unexpectedly.
An assignment to a global variable that is never used has no effect.

rules.cwe_name: Improper Control of Generation of Code ('Code Injection')
rules.description: Invoking user-controlled methods on certain objects can lead to remote code execution.
An array index is compared to be less than or equal to the 'length' property, and then used in an indexing operation that could be out of bounds.

rules.cwe_name: Improper Neutralization of Argument Delimiters in a Command ('Argument Injection')
rules.description: Using externally controlled strings in a command line may allow a malicious user to change the meaning of the command.

rules.cwe_name: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in a Command ('Command Injection')
rules.description: Externally influenced data changes the syntax or meaning of a command sent to a downstream command interpreter.
Deserializing user-controlled data may allow attackers to execute arbitrary code.

rules.cwe_name: Improper Neutralization of Data within XPath Expressions ('XPath Injection')
rules.description: Building an XPath expression from user-controlled sources is vulnerable to insertion of malicious code by the user.
Separately checking the state of a file before operating on it may allow an attacker to modify the file between the two operations.

rules.cwe_name: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an LDAP Query ('LDAP Injection')
rules.description: Building a database query from user-controlled sources is vulnerable to insertion of malicious code by the user.

rules.cwe_name: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')
rules.description: Recursively merging a user-controlled object into another object can allow an attacker to modify the built-in Object prototype, and possibly escalate to remote code execution or cross-site scripting.
Using cookies without CSRF protection may allow malicious websites to submit requests on behalf of the user.
